title: Recycled stream rooms expose a previous caller's bytes to the next fill callback
body:
## A later stream caller can read an earlier caller's bytes from a recycled room

For release tracker #125. @johnservil @devonjonte

A safe-Rust probe with dummy key material found a data-isolation question in the stream API:

1. One caller fills a 64-byte room through `submit_with`, finishes, and its stream scope ends.
2. A later sequential caller on the same thread opens a stream and inspects its room **before overwriting it**, which the `fill(at, room)` closure can do.
3. It observes all 64 bytes left by the first caller.

This reproduces natively and under Miri on:

- main `c75daebf383820e73bbe366d9e770d6168b236e6`;
- two-kinds API `87ab0a283058f4508a41c9476585f69653a2a6cd`.

No Miri UB was reported. This is not a memory-corruption, concurrency or cross-process finding. The issue is the API contract: stream storage is process-global and recycled, while the current docs say the caller writes the room but do not state that its initial contents are unspecified or may contain earlier stream data.

Please decide the supported contract before release:

- document initial contents as unspecified/potentially prior stream data, and state what a caller handling secrets must overwrite or clear; or
- clear used rooms at a defined lifecycle point; or
- another owner-approved isolation design.

I have not chosen a fix or measured the cost of clearing. Clearing could affect the performance-oriented stream path, so it needs an explicit design/performance acceptance decision rather than an unexamined patch. If documentation is chosen, the same initial-content rule should be explicit for `submit_with` and `submit_batch_with` on both Rust API forms and any C exposure of those rooms.

[Probe, source pins, native/Miri logs and dual-hash manifests](https://github.com/samshackleton-tech/BLAKE3/tree/c9a298bd7e0d3b2ae6e8aee56a7413381e189fb4/capi-guards-ring-20261025). Dummy material only; no real secrets or cross-process data were used.

— Sam Shackleton
